$comment: The Rite (design doc §7): each region's staged offering ritual and the Migration gate. Run 1 is authored here; runs 2+ come from the generator (Phase 4) using this as the template. A verse completes when chooseCount of its five slots are filled; slots are weighted so the spotlight crafts are the cheapest path. Resource offerings credit Renown at trade value; deed/specimen/fragment slots carry a fixed renownGrant, and so do resource slots offering unsellable MATERIALS (ingots, cordage — trade value is zero, the validator enforces the grant; values approximate amount x the material's notional input-derived worth). Verse lines live in dialogue.json (verses), verse sites in zones.json (verseSite). Quantities are first-pass — tune in Phase 3 against the §8 pacing targets.
$zoneRampNote: Goods amounts carry a GEOMETRIC zone ramp: x3.5 per zone order, anchored at zone 2 (zone 3 x3.5, 4 x12, 5 x43, 6 x150, 7 x525, rounded clean). The within-run power curve grows ~x2.5 per zone step — each later zone debuts against more stacked tool mults, more banked Verdure and more kith slots — so the ask outruns it by ~x1.4 per verse ON PURPOSE: at x2.5 the ramp merely held each debut verse level with the last (~20-40 min of its own node's production), and a Rite whose verses all cost the same is a Rite with no shape. At x3.5 each verse asks about half again as long as the one before, so verse 7 is the run's event and not its seventh errand. demandGrowth^m stacks on top as the fold-over-fold stretch. Zones 1-2 are pinned by the hour-one pacing targets (verse 1 ~30 min) — do not ramp them. Material-slot renownGrants scale WITH their amounts (grant ~ amount x notional worth, the no-tax promise); deed/specimen/sketch slots stay authored — they price in taps and luck, and the generator scales only their grants. Zones 4-7 never play from this table (fold-gated past run 1) — their rows exist as the generator's value anchors. Ramp is model-derived 2026-07-31, NOT playtested — the run-3-to-run-6 sitting judges it, and it pushes the full-map estimate out past the FTP ~9-12 d / paid ~4-6 d that the x2.5 pass was measured against.
$spreadNote: Amounts also carry the generator's valueSpread (0.7) so this table and the generated Rites read the same way. A pure value split (spread 1) asks 5 copper ingots beside 400 nuts — true to the worth, but the two numbers say nothing to each other, and no player reads 'one ingot = eighty nuts' off a verse card. Softening towards each verse's own geometric-mean worth pulls the counts together (spreads here fall from 80-100x to 17-30x). It is value-NEUTRAL per verse by construction: what the dear slots gain, the cheap slots give up, so this knob never doubles as a difficulty lever. The cost is that a dear slot is no longer worth the same as a cheap one — expect the cheapest slots to be the popular answer, and watch whether choose-3-of-5 still poses a decision when the run-3-to-run-6 sitting happens.

generator.$comment: Run-2+ generator tuning (design §8: verseDemand(m) = baseQty · d^m, spotlight slots cheapest). demandGrowth is d; spotlight slots price at value × spotlightDiscount, off-spotlight at value × offSpotlightPremium. d is tuned against the fold's power ratio, not picked freely. A fold multiplies production by (1 + 0.02·Verdure) and Verdure is a square root of lifetime Renown, so that ratio starts near 3x across the first folds and settles at 1.10-1.15x from fold 7 on. d must sit just above the settled ratio: below it the gate stops gating, far above it the gate walls, because exponential demand always beats a power curve that is asymptotically linear. At the old 2.5 the twelfth fold asked ~1000x the wall-clock of the first; at 1.45 it asks ~2.5x, and folds 2-8 still run faster than the first (which is the prestige promise). spotlightDiscount / offSpotlightPremium are still first guesses.
generator.$valueSpreadNote: How hard a good's own worth divides its slot's value into a unit count: amount = target / (unit^spread x pivot^(1-spread)), pivot being the geometric mean worth of that verse's picks. 1 is the pure value split that produced '260 glow salve or 20000 berry preserves' — the same offering twice over, in two numbers that look nothing alike. 0.7 cuts that gap to about a fifth of what it was while keeping the dearest slot within ~4x the cheapest in value, which is the same order as the spotlight lever (0.6 / 1.5), so the choose-3-of-5 decision survives. Push it lower for legibility and the cheap slots simply win; 0.5 would make the dear slot cost ~9x the cheap one. Value-neutral per verse — see $spreadNote.
generator.$breadthNote: The fold gate grows in BREADTH, not depth. Every second migration a verse asks for one more filled slot (chooseCount + m/chooseCountPerMigrations, capped at chooseCountMax), and the generator adds a goods slot in step so the choice margin the authored Rite has (5 slots, choose 3) never narrows. Breadth costs stationing, kith slots and map coverage rather than wait-time, and it is BOUNDED by how many slots a verse has — so unlike a quantity multiplier it can never outrun the player's power curve. The per-verse clamp in Rite.RequiredSlots is the real guarantee: a verse always keeps at least one slot of choice even where a lean zone gives the generator too few candidates to widen.
